title: PostgreSQL
description: What queries were made, how long they took, and what resources the database is using, from postgres-exporter (Prometheus) over the selected time range, plus the point-in-time SQL diagnostics that used to be the DB Query Performance and DB Size & Retention dashboards: live activity, sizes and retention, indexes, statistics health. Rows 5 to 7 are collapsed and run no queries until opened. How to read it: docs/postgres-query-performance.md.

list.name: exclude
list.label: Exclude roles
list.description: Postgres roles whose statements are left out of the Top queries table. postgres_exporter is the monitoring itself; grafana_reader is this Grafana's own dashboards. The per-role charts always show every role.

panels.title: Exporter
panels.description: Whether postgres-exporter could connect to PostgreSQL on its last scrape.

panels.title: Connections in use
panels.description: All connections to $datname as a share of max_connections.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of block reads served from shared_buffers (5m). Sustained < 95% means reads are going to disk: consider raising shared_buffers.

panels.title: Mean query latency
panels.description: Average execution time per statement over the last 5 minutes, all users.

panels.title: Longest transaction
panels.description: Duration of the oldest open transaction. Long idle-in-transaction sessions block autovacuum and hold locks.

panels.title: WAL size
panels.description: Current size of the write-ahead log (cluster-wide). Grows between checkpoints; sustained growth beyond max_wal_size means checkpoints or archiving are not keeping up.

panels.title: Disk space remaining
panels.description: Free space on the smallest real filesystem (ext4/xfs/btrfs) of the host the database runs on, via node-exporter. When this runs out, postgres stops accepting writes — plan capacity against the Database size and Table bloat tiles.

panels.title: Table bloat
panels.description: Estimated dead space across all user tables — space held by updated/deleted rows that vacuum has not reclaimed yet, computed from planner statistics (needs a recent ANALYZE). Steady growth means autovacuum is not keeping up.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(wastedbytes), 0)::bigint AS value FROM (SELECT
  schemaname, tablename,
  MAX(tbloat) AS tbloat,
  MAX(wastedbytes) AS wastedbytes,
  SUM(wastedibytes) AS wastedibytes,
  MAX(wastedbytes) + SUM(wastedibytes) AS total_wasted
FROM (
SELECT
  schemaname, tablename,
  ROUND((CASE WHEN otta=0 THEN 0.0 ELSE sml.relpages::float/otta END)::numeric,1) AS tbloat,
  CASE WHEN relpages < otta THEN 0 ELSE bs*(sml.relpages-otta)::bigint END AS wastedbytes,
  CASE WHEN ipages < iotta THEN 0 ELSE bs*(ipages-iotta) END AS wastedibytes
FROM (
  SELECT
    schemaname, tablename, cc.reltuples, cc.relpages, bs,
    CEIL((cc.reltuples*((datahdr+ma-
      (CASE WHEN datahdr%ma=0 THEN ma ELSE datahdr%ma END))+nullhdr2+4))/(bs-20::float)) AS otta,
    COALESCE(c2.relname,'?') AS iname, COALESCE(c2.reltuples,0) AS ituples, COALESCE(c2.relpages,0) AS ipages,
    COALESCE(CEIL((c2.reltuples*(datahdr-12))/(bs-20::float)),0) AS iotta
  FROM (
    SELECT
      ma,bs,schemaname,tablename,
      (datawidth+(hdr+ma-(case when hdr%ma=0 THEN ma ELSE hdr%ma END)))::numeric AS datahdr,
      (maxfracsum*(nullhdr+ma-(case when nullhdr%ma=0 THEN ma ELSE nullhdr%ma END))) AS nullhdr2
    FROM (
      SELECT
        schemaname, tablename, hdr, ma, bs,
        SUM((1-null_frac)*avg_width) AS datawidth,
        MAX(null_frac) AS maxfracsum,
        hdr+(
          SELECT 1+count(*)/8
          FROM pg_stats s2
          WHERE null_frac<>0 AND s2.schemaname = s.schemaname AND s2.tablename = s.tablename
        ) AS nullhdr
      FROM pg_stats s, (
        SELECT
          (SELECT current_setting('block_size')::numeric) AS bs,
          CASE WHEN substring(v,12,3) IN ('8.0','8.1','8.2') THEN 27 ELSE 23 END AS hdr,
          CASE WHEN v ~ 'mingw32' THEN 8 ELSE 4 END AS ma
        FROM (SELECT version() AS v) AS foo
      ) AS constants
      GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
    ) AS foo
  ) AS rs
  JOIN pg_class cc ON cc.relname = rs.tablename
  JOIN pg_namespace nn ON cc.relnamespace = nn.oid AND nn.nspname = rs.schemaname AND nn.nspname <> 'information_schema'
  LEFT JOIN pg_index i ON indrelid = cc.oid
  LEFT JOIN pg_class c2 ON c2.oid = i.indexrelid
) AS sml
) AS per_index
WHERE schemaname NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema')
GROUP BY schemaname, tablename
) t

panels.title: Since last autovacuum
panels.description: Time since the autovacuum daemon last vacuumed any user table — reclaiming the dead space shown in the bloat numbers.

panels.title: Since last autoanalyze
panels.description: Time since autovacuum last analyzed any user table. The bloat figures are estimated from these statistics, so a stale value here means stale bloat numbers.

panels.title: Deadlocks (24h)
panels.description: Deadlocks detected in the last 24 hours, regardless of the selected time range. Any value above zero means transactions are locking the same rows in conflicting order — check the postgres log for the queries involved.

panels.title: Forced checkpoints (24h)
panels.description: Checkpoints forced in the last 24 hours because WAL filled up before the scheduled checkpoint (cluster-wide, fixed window). Frequent forced checkpoints cause write stalls and mean max_wal_size is too small for the write volume; occasional ones (e.g. during a backup or manual CHECKPOINT) are harmless.

panels.title: Host CPU usage
panels.description: CPU usage of the host the database runs on (all cores averaged), via node-exporter. Sustained high values slow every query; check whether it is postgres or the app by comparing with 'Where the time goes'.

blk_read_time as a share of active_time (PG14), both cumulative since the database stats reset. Needs track_io_timing=on (the io_timing tile; off on dev, so the share reads 0). 44 % on prod on 2026-09-02: nearly half of all statement time was waiting for disk reads.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(100.0 * blks_hit / NULLIF(blks_hit + blks_read, 0), 2) AS cache_hit_pct, round((100.0 * blk_read_time / NULLIF(active_time, 0))::numeric, 1) AS read_wait_pct, current_setting('track_io_timing') AS io_timing, temp_files, temp_bytes, stats_reset FROM pg_stat_database WHERE datname = current_database()

panels.title: Read wait, share of active time
Top 20 by total time
panels.description: The statements the database spent the most time executing: where the time went. Selected time range and database; roles chosen in the Exclude roles dropdown are left out. Click a header to re-sort these 20.

targets.expr: (sum by (queryid, user) (increase(pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="$datname", user!~"^($exclude)$"}[$__range])) and (topk(20, sum by (queryid, user) (increase(pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="$datname", user!~"^($exclude)$"}[$__range])) > 0))) or label_replace(vector(0), "queryid", "none", "", "")

(sum by (queryid, user) (increase(pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="$datname", user!~"^($exclude)$"}[$__range])) and (topk(20, sum by (queryid, user) (increase(pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="$datname", user!~"^($exclude)$"}[$__range])) > 0))) or label_replace(vector(0), "queryid", "none", "", "")

(sum by (queryid, user) (increase(pg_stat_statements_rows_total{datname="$datname", user!~"^($exclude)$"}[$__range])) and (topk(20, sum by (queryid, user) (increase(pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="$datname", user!~"^($exclude)$"}[$__range])) > 0))) or label_replace(vector(0), "queryid", "none", "", "")

targets.rawSql:
SELECT s.queryid::text AS queryid,
       min(left(regexp_replace(s.query, '\s+', ' ', 'g'), 200)) AS query
FROM pg_stat_statements s
JOIN pg_database d ON d.oid = s.dbid
WHERE d.datname = '${datname}'
GROUP BY s.queryid
ORDER BY max(s.total_exec_time) DESC
LIMIT 1000

Selected time range and database; roles chosen in the Exclude roles dropdown are left out. Click a header to re-sort these 20.

panels.title: Query rate by database user
panels.description: Statements per second by role. Separating ingestion (app role), dashboards (grafana_reader) and monitoring (postgres_exporter) is the point of the role split.

panels.title: Mean query latency by database user
panels.description: Average execution time per statement, 5m window. A rising trend with an unchanged query mix points at table growth, bloat or a plan regression.

panels.title: Where the time goes
panels.description: Execution-seconds per second. Read/write wait requires track_io_timing=on. A large read share means the working set does not fit in cache or a plan is scanning too much.

Time spent waiting for blocks from disk (needs track_io_timing=on; empty on dev). High stddev_ms plus high io_share_pct is the cold-cache signature: the plan is fine, the pages are not in memory. Cumulative since the pg_stat_statements reset shown in the Database & statistics health row; entries can be evicted; statements cancelled before completion (Grafana timeouts) never appear here, see docs/postgres-query-performance.md for the log recipe. Rows group parameter-count variants of one query (IN lists, multi-row VALUES); stddev_ms, where shown, is the max over variants. Transaction-control and session-setting statements and this dashboard's own catalog queries are excluded; on prod, track_utility=off also hides DDL, VACUUM and REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW (those still reach the slow log). Roles chosen in the Exclude roles dropdown are left out.

targets.rawSql: WITH info AS ( SELECT GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - stats_reset)) / 86400, 1.0 / 24) AS days FROM pg_stat_statements_info ), s AS ( SELECT regexp_replace(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(query, '\$\d+', '?', 'g'), 'IN \((\?,\s*)*\?\)', 'IN (...)', 'g'), ' VALUES \((\?,\s*)*\?\)(,\s*\((\?,\s*)*\?\))*', ' VALUES (...)', 'g') AS family, userid, calls, total_exec_time, max_exec_time, stddev_exec_time, rows, shared_blks_hit, shared_blks_read, blk_read_time, temp_blks_read, temp_blks_written FROM pg_stat_statements WHERE dbid = (SELECT oid FROM pg_database WHERE datname = current_database()) AND query !~* '^\s*(SAVEPOINT|RELEASE|ROLLBACK|BEGIN|COMMIT|SET |SHOW |DEALLOCATE|DISCARD)' AND query !~ 'pg_stat_|pg_statio_|pg_blocking_pids|pg_constraint' AND NOT (userid::regrole::text = ANY (ARRAY[${exclude:sqlstring}]::text[])) ) SELECT sum(calls) AS calls, round(sum(blk_read_time)::numeric / 1000, 1) AS io_read_s, round((100.0 * sum(blk_read_time) / NULLIF(sum(total_exec_time), 0))::numeric, 1) AS io_share_pct, round(100.0 * sum(shared_blks_hit) / NULLIF(sum(shared_blks_hit) + sum(shared_blks_read), 0), 1) AS hit_pct, round((sum(total_exec_time) / NULLIF(sum(calls), 0))::numeric, 2) AS mean_ms, round(max(stddev_exec_time)::numeric, 1) AS stddev_ms, string_agg(DISTINCT userid::regrole::text, ',') AS role, left(regexp_replace(family, '\s+', ' ', 'g'), 120) AS query FROM s GROUP BY family HAVING sum(blk_read_time) > 0 ORDER BY sum(blk_read_time) DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Top 20 by I/O read time
Connections by state
panels.description: 'idle in transaction' piling up usually means an application bug; approaching max_connections needs pooling.

panels.title: Temp file writes
panels.description: Sorts and hashes spilling to disk because they exceed work_mem.

panels.title: Temp spill, selected range
panels.description: Temp files created and bytes written to them within the selected time range: sorts and hashes that did not fit in work_mem. Occasional spill from a large one-off query is normal; a steady non-zero value means a frequent query spills on every run. The statement is in the db log under 'temporary file' (prod logs every temp file over log_temp_files).

Statements that spilled sorts or hashes to disk: work_mem was too small for them. Cumulative since the pg_stat_statements reset shown in the Database & statistics health row; entries can be evicted; statements cancelled before completion (Grafana timeouts) never appear here, see docs/postgres-query-performance.md for the log recipe. Rows group parameter-count variants of one query (IN lists, multi-row VALUES); stddev_ms, where shown, is the max over variants. Transaction-control and session-setting statements and this dashboard's own catalog queries are excluded; on prod, track_utility=off also hides DDL, VACUUM and REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW (those still reach the slow log). Roles chosen in the Exclude roles dropdown are left out.

targets.rawSql: WITH info AS ( SELECT GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - stats_reset)) / 86400, 1.0 / 24) AS days FROM pg_stat_statements_info ), s AS ( SELECT regexp_replace(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(query, '\$\d+', '?', 'g'), 'IN \((\?,\s*)*\?\)', 'IN (...)', 'g'), ' VALUES \((\?,\s*)*\?\)(,\s*\((\?,\s*)*\?\))*', ' VALUES (...)', 'g') AS family, userid, calls, total_exec_time, max_exec_time, stddev_exec_time, rows, shared_blks_hit, shared_blks_read, blk_read_time, temp_blks_read, temp_blks_written FROM pg_stat_statements WHERE dbid = (SELECT oid FROM pg_database WHERE datname = current_database()) AND query !~* '^\s*(SAVEPOINT|RELEASE|ROLLBACK|BEGIN|COMMIT|SET |SHOW |DEALLOCATE|DISCARD)' AND query !~ 'pg_stat_|pg_statio_|pg_blocking_pids|pg_constraint' AND NOT (userid::regrole::text = ANY (ARRAY[${exclude:sqlstring}]::text[])) ) SELECT sum(calls) AS calls, (sum(temp_blks_written) * current_setting('block_size')::bigint)::bigint AS temp_written, (sum(temp_blks_read) * current_setting('block_size')::bigint)::bigint AS temp_read, (sum(temp_blks_written) * current_setting('block_size')::bigint / NULLIF(sum(calls), 0))::bigint AS temp_per_call, round((sum(total_exec_time) / NULLIF(sum(calls), 0))::numeric, 2) AS mean_ms, string_agg(DISTINCT userid::regrole::text, ',') AS role, left(regexp_replace(family, '\s+', ' ', 'g'), 120) AS query FROM s GROUP BY family HAVING sum(temp_blks_written) > 0 ORDER BY sum(temp_blks_written) DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Top 20 by temp written

panels.description: Live client-backend counts from pg_stat_activity (autovacuum, parallel and WAL workers excluded). idle_in_txn holds locks and blocks vacuum; waiting_on_lock is contention right now; client_backends_pct is client backends over max_connections.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE state = 'active') AS active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE state = 'idle') AS idle, count(*) FILTER (WHERE state LIKE 'idle in transaction%') AS idle_in_txn, count(*) FILTER (WHERE wait_event_type = 'Lock') AS waiting_on_lock, round(100.0 * count(*) / current_setting('max_connections')::int, 1) AS client_backends_pct, current_setting('max_connections')::int AS max_connections FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE backend_type = 'client backend' AND pid <> pg_backend_pid()

panels.title: Backends

panels.description: Client backends whose current statement started more than 2 s ago, oldest first. Includes 'idle in transaction' sessions on purpose: for those, age_s is time since their last statement, and a long idle transaction blocks vacuum. Text cut at 120 characters. Empty is the normal state. Roles chosen in the Exclude roles dropdown are left out.

targets.rawSql: SELECT pid, usename AS role, COALESCE(NULLIF(application_name, ''), '-') AS app, COALESCE(host(client_addr), 'local') AS client, state, COALESCE(wait_event_type || ':' || wait_event, '-') AS wait, round(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - query_start))::numeric, 1) AS age_s, left(regexp_replace(query, '\s+', ' ', 'g'), 120) AS query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE backend_type = 'client backend' AND state <> 'idle' AND pid <> pg_backend_pid() AND now() - query_start > interval '2 seconds' AND NOT (usename::text = ANY (ARRAY[${exclude:sqlstring}]::text[])) ORDER BY query_start

panels.title: Statements running longer than 2 s

panels.description: Sessions waiting on a lock held by another session (pg_blocking_pids). blocked_by lists the holder pids; find them in the panel above. Empty is the normal state. Roles chosen in the Exclude roles dropdown are left out.

targets.rawSql: SELECT a.pid, array_to_string(pg_blocking_pids(a.pid), ',') AS blocked_by, a.usename AS role, COALESCE(a.wait_event_type || ':' || a.wait_event, '-') AS wait, round(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - a.query_start))::numeric, 1) AS age_s, left(regexp_replace(a.query, '\s+', ' ', 'g'), 120) AS query FROM pg_stat_activity a WHERE cardinality(pg_blocking_pids(a.pid)) > 0 AND NOT (a.usename::text = ANY (ARRAY[${exclude:sqlstring}]::text[])) ORDER BY a.query_start

panels.title: Blocked sessions

panels.description: Top 20 tables by total size (heap + indexes + toast). est_rows is from planner statistics (pg_class.reltuples) and is refreshed by autovacuum/ANALYZE.

targets.rawSql: SELECT n.nspname || '.' || c.relname AS "table", pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(c.oid)) AS total, pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(c.oid)) AS heap, pg_size_pretty(pg_indexes_size(c.oid)) AS indexes, pg_size_pretty(COALESCE(pg_total_relation_size(c.reltoastrelid),0)) AS toast, to_char(c.reltuples, 'FM999,999,999,999') AS est_rows FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE c.relkind IN ('r','m') AND n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(c.oid) DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Top 20 tables by total size

panels.description: Per-table row count, heap size, and average bytes per row. Avg bytes per row separates 'big because of row count' from 'big because of wide rows / TOAST'. est_rows is the planner estimate (pg_class.reltuples).

targets.rawSql: SELECT n.nspname || '.' || c.relname AS "table", to_char(c.reltuples, 'FM999,999,999,999') AS est_rows, pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(c.oid)) AS heap, pg_size_pretty((pg_relation_size(c.oid) / NULLIF(c.reltuples, 0))::bigint) AS avg_bytes_per_row FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE c.relkind = 'r' AND n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') ORDER BY pg_relation_size(c.oid) DESC LIMIT 30

panels.title: Rows / bytes-per-row / size (all tables)

panels.description: For each major time-stamped table: how long have we been collecting (age_days), how big has the table become, and the implied average growth rate. Assumes roughly linear growth from oldest record to now — a useful sanity check, not a forecast. To track actual growth over time, see docs/todo.md → 'Add postgres_exporter for time-series DB observability'.

targets.rawSql: WITH per_table(label, tname, oldest) AS (VALUES ('extrinsics','extrinsics',(SELECT MIN(created_at) FROM extrinsics)), ('metagraph_block','metagraph_block',(SELECT MIN(timestamp) FROM metagraph_block)), ('metagraph_dump','metagraph_dump',(SELECT MIN(finished_at) FROM metagraph_dump WHERE finished_at IS NOT NULL)), ('subnet_hyperparam_history','subnet_hyperparam_history',(SELECT MIN(created_at) FROM subnet_hyperparam_history))) SELECT pt.label AS "table", EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM pt.oldest) * 1000 AS oldest, (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - pt.oldest)) / 86400)::int AS age_days, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(format('public.%I', pt.tname)::regclass)) AS total_size, round(pg_total_relation_size(format('public.%I', pt.tname)::regclass)::numeric / NULLIF(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - pt.oldest))/86400, 0) / 1024 / 1024, 2) AS mb_per_day, round(pg_total_relation_size(format('public.%I', pt.tname)::regclass)::numeric / NULLIF(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - pt.oldest))/86400, 0) / 1024 / 1024 * 365, 0) AS mb_per_year_projected FROM per_table pt WHERE pt.oldest IS NOT NULL ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(format('public.%I', pt.tname)::regclass) DESC

panels.title: Retention focus (per major table)

panels.description: Definitive gaps for parent-row deletes and reverse lookups: no valid, non-partial index has the FK columns as its leading key columns. Empty is good. A row whose in_other_index is set means the column is indexed but not as the leading column, or only by a partial index: acceptable while parent_deletes stays 0 and nothing queries by that column alone. On prod the two rows (metagraph_bond and metagraph_weight target_neuron_id) are deliberate drops from migration 0007.

targets.rawSql: SELECT c.conrelid::regclass::text AS "table", string_agg(a.attname, ',' ORDER BY x.n) AS columns, c.confrelid::regclass::text AS "references", pg_relation_size(c.conrelid) AS size, (SELECT string_agg(i.indexrelid::regclass::text, ',') FROM pg_index i WHERE i.indrelid = c.conrelid AND i.indkey::smallint[] @> c.conkey) AS in_other_index, (SELECT n_tup_del FROM pg_stat_user_tables t WHERE t.relid = c.confrelid) AS parent_deletes FROM pg_constraint c CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(c.conkey) WITH ORDINALITY AS x(attnum, n) JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = c.conrelid AND a.attnum = x.attnum WHERE c.contype = 'f' AND NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM pg_index i WHERE i.indrelid = c.conrelid AND i.indisvalid AND i.indpred IS NULL AND i.indnkeyatts >= cardinality(c.conkey) AND (i.indkey::smallint[])[0:cardinality(c.conkey) - 1] @> c.conkey AND (i.indkey::smallint[])[0:cardinality(c.conkey) - 1] <@ c.conkey ) GROUP BY c.conrelid, c.conname, c.confrelid, c.conkey ORDER BY pg_relation_size(c.conrelid) DESC

panels.title: Foreign keys without a leading-column index

panels.description: Every query the left index serves can use one of covered_by: same access method, operator classes, collations and ordering, and the left index's key columns are a leading prefix of the right one (or an exact duplicate, such as a leftover from an interrupted REINDEX CONCURRENTLY). Unique, primary, partial and expression indexes are never listed as redundant, and invalid indexes never count as cover. Dropping one trades a slightly wider index per lookup for less write amplification and disk. Django creates one automatically per ForeignKey; a unique_together on the same leading column makes it redundant. Prod 2026-09-03: 23 indexes, 8.5 GB.

targets.rawSql: SELECT a.indrelid::regclass::text AS "table", a.indexrelid::regclass::text AS redundant_index, string_agg(b.indexrelid::regclass::text, ', ' ORDER BY b.indnatts, b.indexrelid::regclass::text) AS covered_by, pg_relation_size(a.indexrelid) AS size, sa.idx_scan FROM pg_index a JOIN pg_index b ON b.indrelid = a.indrelid AND b.indexrelid <> a.indexrelid JOIN pg_class ca ON ca.oid = a.indexrelid JOIN pg_class cb ON cb.oid = b.indexrelid JOIN pg_stat_user_indexes sa ON sa.indexrelid = a.indexrelid WHERE ca.relam = cb.relam AND a.indpred IS NULL AND b.indpred IS NULL AND a.indexprs IS NULL AND b.indexprs IS NULL AND b.indisvalid AND NOT a.indisprimary AND NOT a.indisunique AND b.indnkeyatts >= a.indnkeyatts AND (b.indnatts > a.indnatts OR (b.indnatts = a.indnatts AND (b.indisunique OR a.indexrelid > b.indexrelid))) AND array_to_string((b.indkey::smallint[])[0:a.indnatts - 1], ',') = array_to_string(a.indkey::smallint[], ',') AND array_to_string((b.indclass::oid[])[0:a.indnatts - 1], ',') = array_to_string(a.indclass::oid[], ',') AND array_to_string((b.indoption::smallint[])[0:a.indnatts - 1], ',') = array_to_string(a.indoption::smallint[], ',') AND array_to_string((b.indcollation::oid[])[0:a.indnatts - 1], ',') = array_to_string(a.indcollation::oid[], ',') GROUP BY a.indrelid, a.indexrelid, sa.idx_scan ORDER BY pg_relation_size(a.indexrelid) DESC

panels.title: Redundant indexes

panels.description: When the postgres stat counters were last reset (manual reset, restart, or crash). idx_scan = 0 for indexes created after this time means 'truly unused'; before this time it could mean 'we forgot.' As a rule of thumb, don't trust the Unused panel until at least a week after this timestamp.

targets.rawSql: SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM stats_reset) * 1000 AS reset_at FROM pg_stat_database WHERE datname = current_database()

panels.title: Stats counters last reset

panels.description: Indexes that have never been scanned. Unique and primary-key indexes are excluded — they enforce constraints even when they have no scan activity. Read with the 'Stats counters last reset' panel above: an idx_scan of 0 only means 'unused' if enough time has passed since the reset.

targets.rawSql: SELECT s.schemaname || '.' || s.relname AS "table", s.indexrelname AS index, pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(s.indexrelid)) AS size FROM pg_stat_user_indexes s JOIN pg_index i ON i.indexrelid = s.indexrelid WHERE s.idx_scan = 0 AND NOT i.indisunique AND NOT i.indisprimary ORDER BY pg_relation_size(s.indexrelid) DESC

panels.title: Unused indexes (idx_scan = 0)

panels.description: Indexes that get scanned but are large relative to their usage. A big index with a small scans count is a candidate for review — either it's overly broad (consider partial / smaller composite), or it serves a rare query that doesn't justify the size.

targets.rawSql: SELECT s.schemaname || '.' || s.relname AS "table", s.indexrelname AS index, s.idx_scan AS scans, pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(s.indexrelid)) AS size, s.idx_tup_read, s.idx_tup_fetch FROM pg_stat_user_indexes s JOIN pg_index i ON i.indexrelid = s.indexrelid WHERE s.idx_scan > 0 AND NOT i.indisunique AND NOT i.indisprimary ORDER BY pg_relation_size(s.indexrelid) DESC LIMIT 30

panels.title: Low-scan indexes by size

panels.description: Cumulative since the database stats reset. A handful of scans each reading hundreds of millions of rows is the signature of an unindexed dashboard query. Cancelled queries still count here even though they never reach pg_stat_statements. Small lookup tables are filtered out on purpose.

targets.rawSql: SELECT relname AS "table", pg_relation_size(relid) AS size, seq_scan, seq_tup_read, round(seq_tup_read::numeric / NULLIF(seq_scan, 0)) AS rows_per_seq_scan, COALESCE(idx_scan, 0) AS idx_scan, round(100.0 * seq_scan / NULLIF(seq_scan + COALESCE(idx_scan, 0), 0), 1) AS seq_scan_pct, n_live_tup FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE pg_relation_size(relid) > 100 * 1024 * 1024 AND seq_scan > 0 ORDER BY seq_tup_read DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Sequential scans on tables over 100 MB

panels.description: Top 30 indexes by on-disk size. Useful for spotting bloated or over-broad indexes.

targets.rawSql: SELECT schemaname || '.' || tablename AS "table", indexname, pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(format('%I.%I', schemaname, indexname)::regclass)) AS size, LEFT(indexdef, 120) AS definition FROM pg_indexes WHERE schemaname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') ORDER BY pg_relation_size(format('%I.%I', schemaname, indexname)::regclass) DESC LIMIT 30

panels.title: Top 30 indexes by size

panels.description: idx_blks_read counts index pages fetched from outside shared_buffers (OS cache or disk), cumulative since the database stats reset. Cost, not coverage: which indexes are cold. On prod, random-key inserts into the large unique indexes dominate (unique_neuron_block 1.6 TB, unique_bond 1.2 TB at 86 % hit on 2026-09-02).

targets.rawSql: SELECT s.relname AS "table", s.indexrelname AS index, pg_relation_size(s.indexrelid) AS size, s.idx_scan, io.idx_blks_read, round(100.0 * io.idx_blks_hit / NULLIF(io.idx_blks_hit + io.idx_blks_read, 0), 1) AS hit_pct, io.idx_blks_read * current_setting('block_size')::bigint AS read_from_disk FROM pg_stat_user_indexes s JOIN pg_statio_user_indexes io ON io.indexrelid = s.indexrelid WHERE io.idx_blks_read > 0 ORDER BY io.idx_blks_read DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Indexes by blocks read from disk

panels.description: From pg_stat_bgwriter (PG14 to 16 columns; PG17 moves them to pg_stat_checkpointer and pg_stat_io). forced_pct: checkpoints requested rather than timed. WAL volume beyond max_wal_size is the usual cause, but restarts, explicit CHECKPOINT and CREATE DATABASE count too, so a yellow right after a deploy is expected. backend_to_ckpt_ratio: buffers written by backends themselves versus by the checkpointer; above 1 means backends are writing dirty pages, either evictions mid-query or bulk loads through ring buffers (prod was 13x before the August 2026 tuning). buffers_backend_fsync should stay 0.

targets.rawSql: SELECT checkpoints_timed, checkpoints_req, round(100.0 * checkpoints_req / NULLIF(checkpoints_timed + checkpoints_req, 0), 1) AS forced_pct, round(buffers_backend::numeric / NULLIF(buffers_checkpoint, 0), 2) AS backend_to_ckpt_ratio, buffers_backend_fsync, round(checkpoint_write_time / 1000 / 60) AS write_minutes FROM pg_stat_bgwriter

panels.title: Checkpoints & buffers

panels.description: Can the Statement statistics row be trusted? fill_pct near 100 plus growing evictions means rarely run statements are being dropped before anyone sees them. savepoint_pct above 0 means track_utility is still on and Django's uniquely named savepoints are flooding the table (prod: 99.9 % of entries on 2026-09-02). Reset with SELECT pg_stat_statements_reset() after changing the flag.

targets.rawSql: WITH s AS ( SELECT count(*) AS entries, count(*) FILTER (WHERE query ~* '^\s*(SAVEPOINT|RELEASE\s+SAVEPOINT|ROLLBACK\s+TO)') AS savepoints FROM pg_stat_statements ) SELECT s.entries, current_setting('pg_stat_statements.max')::int AS max_entries, round(100.0 * s.entries / current_setting('pg_stat_statements.max')::int, 1) AS fill_pct, i.dealloc AS evictions, round(100.0 * s.savepoints / NULLIF(s.entries, 0), 1) AS savepoint_pct, current_setting('pg_stat_statements.track_utility') AS track_utility, round(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - i.stats_reset)) / 86400, 1) AS days_since_reset FROM pg_stat_statements_info i, s

panels.title: pg_stat_statements health
